Hi Marissa,

We are preparing for our SOC 2 readiness assessment and the assessor has requested artefacts around your Secure SDLC practices. Could you please provide the following items or point us to a bundle we can download?

- Description of your code review policy and enforcement (who approves, required reviews, code owners)
- Evidence of PR gating and branch protection (screenshots or audit export)
- CI/CD pipeline controls and retention policy (build logs, artifact retention, rollback/rollback-testing notes)
- Secrets management: where secrets are stored, rotation cadence, how ephemeral credentials are used in CI
- Change management records for production deployments (Q1 2026)

We are on a tight timeline — assessor would like these by COB Tuesday, 2026-04-14. If anything needs more time, please flag what we can deliver first.

Hi Jane — adding technical details here so the assessor has context for the artifacts we attached. Short summary first, then pointers to the zipped logs.

1) Code review and PR gating- We enforce branch protection on main and release branches via GitHub: required 1 reviewer for library and infra repos, required 2 reviewers for service repos; CODEOWNERS enforced; no direct pushes to protected branches.
- Mandatory status checks: unit test, integration test, SAST (CodeQL) and dependency scan (Snyk) must pass before merges.
- Approvals are audited and exported as CSV (attached).

2) CI/CD controls- Pipelines are authored as YAML in repo (Actions/Jenkins hybrid). Artifacts and logs are retained for 90 days by default; we attach log export for March 2026 and a screenshot of the retention policy.
- Deployments to prod require a tagged release and are gated by an approval step in the pipeline that requires sign-off from the oncall + product manager (tracked in the pipeline UI).
- Rollback: every deployment generates a rollback plan artifact and we exercise rollback in canary jobs during release verification. Runbooks are retained in Confluence (link in related_links).

3) Secrets management- We do not store plaintext secrets in repos. CI uses short-lived tokens provisioned from our KMS (AWS KMS + Vault in dedicated cluster). Secrets in CI are injected via the pipeline runtime as ephemeral credentials, rotated daily for CI runners and quarterly for long-lived service keys.
- Secrets access is audited and logs are retained per our retention policy; redacted logs are in the ZIP.

4) Change management- Changes to production are tracked via Jira change tickets; we export the change-management-log for Q1. Emergency changes require a documented emergency approval and postmortem within 72 hours.

Attachments in ci-cd-pipeline-logs-202603.zip: 
- 03-05-build-logs-redacted.txt
- pipeline-retention-policy-screenshot.png
- deploy-approval-audit-202603.csv

If the assessor wants a live demonstration of the pipeline gating and the secrets injection flow I can do a 20-minute screen share.

—Dev
